title: Southshore Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for production onboarding of Redwood for Southshore Health. Covered timeline, success metrics, infra access (VPC), security requirements (SOC2, KMS, SAML), pilot scope (chat + embeddings), SLAs, and next steps including access handoff, test dataset, and benchmarking windows.
action_items: Sofia: Send onboarding playbook and access checklist by 2027-03-03

Customer to provide test dataset and sample prompts (PII redacted)

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-01 15:00 UTC | Duration: 48m | Recording: yes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Reynolds (Southshore CTO), Ethan Brooks (Head of ML), Priya Kapoor (Security Lead), Jordan Lee (Platform Eng)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on onboarding steps, security, infra access, and pilot KPIs.

00:00 - Sofia Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll do a quick round of intros and then go through the onboarding playbook.
00:14 - Maya Reynolds: Sounds good, yeah we have all here, thanks Sofia. I'm Maya, CTO at Southshore. Our main goals are to get chat assistants into the clinician portal without leaking PHI and to try embeddings for search over our care guidelines.
00:32 - Sofia Martinez: Great. Quick note on goals — we'll call out success criteria: latency target for chat under 300ms per token at 95th percentile, embedding throughput of ~50 req/s for initial pilot, and no customer PII stored in the host logs.
00:49 - Ethan Brooks: Right, latency is the big one. We're also very cost sensitive; if we have to run dedicated all the time it's fine but we need predictability.
01:05 - Arjun Patel: Totally. For that we usually recommend starting on a small Redwood Dedicated pool, run a benchmark, then iterate on batching and KV cache. We can also suggest quantized model variants to reduce GPU usage.
01:22 - Priya Kapoor: On security — we need SOC2 alignment, KMS/HSM integration for key management, and SAML SSO. Also audit logs for every request tied to user IDs. Can Redwood provide those?
01:36 - Liam Chen: Yes, we support SOC2 controls and we have an integration for customer-managed KMS in private deployments; audit logs with per-request metadata are available through the console and can be pushed to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3. We'll share the mapping doc.
01:53 - Jordan Lee: On the network side we prefer VPC peering rather than exposed endpoints. We need to know IP ranges and peering steps so we can open the right fw rules.
02:06 - Arjun Patel: We'll hand over the subnet CIDRs and a peering runbook. For private deployments we can do VPC-only flows and we also have an on-prem option, but that's a longer project.
02:23 - Maya Reynolds: One of our constraints is that we can't send any raw PHI outbound. We need to confirm how Redwood handles tokenization/caching and whether logs can be redacted.
02:37 - Arjun Patel: Understood. We have options to disable request logging or redact tokens. We also have prefix KV cache control; you can choose not to cache any persistent KV for conversation history. We'll document the policies.
02:54 - Ethan Brooks: What's the usual time to get a pilot environment up and running? We want something by mid-March ideally.
03:05 - Sofia Martinez: Mid-March is realistic. Immediate steps: access handoff (account owner and IAM role), VPC peering, and a test dataset. If we get those this week, SE can run a benchmark next week.
03:21 - Maya Reynolds: Okay we'll try to get the peering request in today.

03:37 - (short pause)
03:45 - Liam Chen: I'll follow up after with the pricing/commit detail for Dedicated so you can plan the monthly commit. We can also outline a burst-to-hosted policy for off-peak bursts to save cost.
04:00 - Jordan Lee: That burst thing sounds useful, can you explain how fallback works if Dedicated saturates?
04:10 - Arjun Patel: Fallback routing can route to a compatible hosted variant. There's a small perf delta but it's better than queueing. We also do automatic fallback rules configurable by route.
04:24 - Ethan Brooks: Do you support function/tool calling or structured outputs for the clinician assistant? We want to extract entities for charting.
04:36 - Arjun Patel: Yes, streaming responses and function-calling are supported. We have SDKs which show how to derive structured JSON outputs. Note: sometimes transcription will render the product names slightly off in meeting notes, but the SDK examples are in the repo.
04:54 - Maya Reynolds: On compliance, Priya will lead on our side; Priya, anything else we should ask Redwood?
05:02 - Priya Kapoor: Need to verify key rotation policies, where keys are stored, and whether logs including debug traces can be excluded. Also need an SLA for access to historical logs for audits.
05:15 - Liam Chen: We'll include key rotation best practices and the KMS architecture diagram. We also have an extended retention add-on if you need longer audit trails.
05:29 - Sofia Martinez: Great. Now walk through the onboarding playbook - quick bullets: 1) access & infra 2) pilot scope and dataset 3) benchmark window 4) tweaks & ops runbooks 5) rollout plan.
05:45 - (screen share noted)
06:02 - Arjun Patel: For benchmarks, we'll run three load patterns: steady state throughput for embeddings, conversational bursty traffic for chat, and a long-context test to validate KV cache behavior. We'll collect latency p95/p99 and cost tokens.
06:28 - Ethan Brooks: For the long-context test — any guidance on sequence lengths? Our clinician notes can be long, up to 8k tokens.
06:38 - Arjun Patel: We'll simulate 8k; some model variants have more efficient attention kernels for long context. We can recommend a quantized long-context model if you need lower cost. There may be grammar glitches when we auto-transcribe model names in notes, ha.
06:56 - Maya Reynolds: About model pinning — we want to pin to a specific version during pilot to avoid regressions. How does Redwood handle rollouts?
07:07 - Arjun Patel: You can pin a model version at route level, and do canary rollouts with automatic fallback if QoS drops. The Console shows per-route latency and token costs.
07:20 - Priya Kapoor: Who will have admin access in Redwood console? We need RBAC, SSO mapping to our AD groups.
07:29 - Liam Chen: RBAC is supported; we'll share role templates. We'll work with your SSO admin to map AD groups to Redwood roles.
07:43 - Jordan Lee: Can we have read-only access to logs for our auditors?
07:49 - Liam Chen: Yes, you can provision a read-only role or push logs to your SIEM.
07:56 - (crosstalk) Maya: Okay, next — pilot scope specifics?
08:03 - Sofia Martinez: We propose two pilot routes: 1) clinician assist chat with 95th pct latency target, 2) embeddings search with vector db integration. Pilot length 4 weeks. Success criteria: accuracy on NPS-style evals > 80%, latency targets met, and no log PII.
08:21 - Ethan Brooks: Sounds reasonable. For the embeddings integration, we use Pinecone today, but we're open to running DB in our infra.
08:31 - Arjun Patel: We integrate with common vector stores; we can push vectors to your cluster or you can keep them in your infra. We'll share a connector reference.
08:44 - Maya Reynolds: About cost: do you have rough estimates for the pilot? We need a budget to sign off.
08:52 - Liam Chen: We'll send a pilot cost estimate with Dedicated sizing and an optional burst-to-hosted cost model. Expect an initial estimate by EOD tomorrow.
09:03 - Jordan Lee: Ok, on the VPC peering request I'll need the IP ranges.
09:09 - Sofia Martinez: We'll send the peering CIDRs and the peering template.
09:15 - Maya Reynolds: Any blockers we should flag?
09:18 - Priya Kapoor: If encryption in transit doesn't meet our standards, we'd need a custom link. Also, any third-party subprocessors need to be listed for our procurement.
09:31 - Liam Chen: Procurement usually wants a subcontractor list; we'll include that in the security packet.
09:38 - (brief pause)
09:45 - Arjun Patel: Quick note on observability — Console has per-token cost breakdown, route-level traces, and error analysis. We'll set up dashboards for your SRE.
09:58 - Jordan Lee: Dashboard access would be great.
10:03 - Sofia Martinez: We're going to do a follow-up technical deep dive with Arjun for the SE-led session — goal is to run the first benchmark and walk through KV cache settings. Suggesting week of 2027-03-08.
10:18 - Maya Reynolds: Works for us. We'll aim to have the peering and a small test dataset by then.
10:25 - (screen share ends)
10:33 - Liam Chen: I'll recap the next steps in an email: send playbook, pricing, security docs, peering CIDRs, and set up the SE benchmark slot.
10:45 - Maya Reynolds: Thanks all. Priya, Ethan and Jordan will coordinate the technical requests.
11:00 - Priya Kapoor: We'll get the SOC2 mapping and our internal policies over; expect a doc from procurement soon.
11:10 - Sofia Martinez: Perfect. Any other questions?
11:16 - Ethan Brooks: One quick one — what's the rollback behavior if a model update causes hallucinations or regression?
11:24 - Arjun Patel: We do instant rollback to the previous pinned variant, and you can configure automatic regression alerts tied to evaluation prompts. We also keep model artifacts per version for audit.
11:38 - Maya Reynolds: Great. If no more questions, let's close.
11:45 - Sofia Martinez: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the items we discussed.

Meeting end: 15:48 UTC

Notes / Artifacts referenced: onboarding_playbook.pdf (link sent in follow-up), security_packet_v2.pdf, peering_template.xlsx, pilot_pricing_estimate.xlsx

Transcript quality notes: auto-generated; some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (e.g., Redwood Private / Redwood Dedicated transcribed inconsistently).

Recap (auto): 1) Redwood to send playbook, peering details, pricing and security docs. 2) Southshore to submit VPC peering and sample dataset. 3) Schedule SE benchmark week of 2027-03-08.
